Subject: Private deployment - operator access & certification requests

Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week — NuvemHealth is keen to move forward on the dedicated VPC pilot. Before we get the PO signed we need to confirm a couple of items that our infosec procurement team flagged. I realise some are sensitive so appreciate a quick confirmation of what Redwood can commit to in the MSA/order form: 

- Operator access boundary: we need a one-paragraph description suitable for our security team explaining the conditions under which Redwood engineers may access the environment (triggered incidents, scheduled maintenance), whether access is agent-based or direct SSH, and the approval workflow.
- Evidence of snapshot/proof-of-execution: for our auditors we require a lightweight attestation process showing a snapshot of a model container + manifest and the time-limited credentials used by operators (redacted). A simple template or example output would be ideal.
- Custody / escrow-like ask: if we need an exit (regulatory or acquisition), what evidence/custody options are on the table short of full source escrow? Our lawyers mentioned a custody affirmation or signed image snapshot transfer; curious if Redwood has a standard approach.

I've attached our "ops requirements" doc that surfaced these asks. Can you route this to legal and security and get back with proposed contract language or acceptable alternatives? We hope to close by end of month.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Cho
Head of Platform Security, NuvemHealth

Thanks Daniel — great summary and the doc is helpful. Looping in Legal (Laura) and InfoSec (Priya) to propose language and an evidence workflow. High-level responses below; we can follow with concrete redlines and a short telecon if helpful.

Summary answers (high-level):
- Operator access: Redwood does not use blanket SSH access. Operator actions are performed via our audited admin console and ephemeral operator sessions with time-limited credentials. For critical incidents we can provide documented approvals and session recordings for a 90‑day window.
- Snapshot attestation: we can provide a signed snapshot manifest (SHA‑256 hashes + container metadata) and a short "proof of execution" package that includes timestamped logs and the signing certificate chain. We generally avoid transferring private keys; instead we provide a signed artifact verifiable by your auditors.
- Custody alternatives: we have a standard "escrow-lite" pathway — not full source code escrow, but an operator-handover and artifact-transfer protocol that includes notarised manifests and a snapshot transfer executed under an agreed checklist. Will propose clause text.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) Laura to provide contract redline suggestions for the MSA/order form (operator access boundary, evidence delivery SLA, custody pathway).
2) Priya to prepare a short sample "proof_of_snapshot_template.pdf" that demonstrates the signed manifest and what fields are included.
3) I'll schedule a 30-minute call this week to agree scope and timing — propose Thu 25 Mar 10:00 PT.

If any of the above items are deal-breakers please flag immediately. We'll aim to keep the obligations scoped so we don't expose unnecessary operational detail in the MSA.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez

Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Below are proposed contract positions that should be sufficient for procurement while limiting operational exposure. I'm marking two optional items as "customer-elected" so they are only included if NuvemHealth requires them in the order form.

Proposed contract language (summary):
- "Operator access boundary": Redwood personnel shall only access Customer environments via authenticated, auditable operator sessions initiated through the Redwood administrative console or via pre-scheduled maintenance windows. Emergency access requires an incident ticket, prior written approval from Customer SOC (email ok), and will be recorded. Operator sessions and relevant logs will be retained for 90 days. (Optional: Customer may request 3rd-party session review during onboarding under a mutual NDA.)

- "Evidence of snapshot and proof-of-execution": Redwood will provide, upon Customer request and subject to agreed lead time, a signed artifact including container manifest, image digest (SHA‑256), and timestamped execution logs sufficient for third-party verification. Delivery: within 5 business days after request. (Optional: Redwood can provide notarised transfer of artifacts to an agreed escrow agent for an additional fee.)

- "Custody / escrow-lite pathway": If Customer elects the escrow-lite option, Redwood will deliver a sealed artifact bundle to an agreed neutral escrow agent together with a signed acceptance certificate. The bundle content and release conditions will be defined in an Annex and executed only on specific release triggers (insolvency, long-term failure to meet SLA, or court order). This is not a source code escrow and does not include proprietary build tooling.

I attached a redline (word doc) with line edits for the MSA and an example annex template. A few practical notes:
- We should avoid operationally sensitive enumerations (e.g., exact runtime flags, internal audit endpoint URLs) in contract language; better to define the types of artifacts and SLA.
- For the snapshot proof, we'll deliver signed manifests; if Customer insists on key handback we will require additional indemnities and a separate order.

Please review and let us know which "optional" items you want included. If you confirm escrow-lite, we will get pricing and escrow-agent options.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

- We will take the snapshot attestation as standard (no escrow agent for now) — please produce the proof_of_snapshot_template.pdf and the signed manifest sample. We may request notarised delivery later but want to avoid extra cost for the pilot.
